title: Coupling effect of nearest-neighbor interacting qubit chains to a single qubit system
authors: Manuel Allan L. Orongan, Lemuel John F. Sese, Rayda P. Gammag
abstract: This study establishes a theorem that provides sufficient criteria for identifying terms in any time-independent Hamiltonian that have no influence on local dynamics, local observables, or any local phenomena, without any approximation. The usefulness of this theorem is demonstrated by predicting the behavior of three systems. The first system consists of multiple qubit chains with Ising interactions. The second system is formed by a single qubit chain, differentiated by the substitution of Dzyalonshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction for the last Ising interaction. The predictions were verified by analytically deriving the reduced dynamics of both systems. A third system was also considered, namely, a short qubit chain with a transverse magnetic field on the intermediary environment qubit. This transverse magnetic field signals that the commutation relation required by our theorem no longer holds. The third system's local dynamics were also derived analytically, demonstrating that all Hamiltonian constituents contributed to the reduced dynamics. The physical consequences of our theorem's inapplicability were also explored using this third system by analyzing the entanglement dynamics between the qubits that do not directly interact. The results showed that the entanglement is caused by an \textit{emergent coupling} between the two non-directly interacting subsystems. This \textit{emergent coupling} arises from the non-commutativity of the intermediate interactions connecting the two subsystems. When searching for these \textit{emergent couplings}, our theorem can eliminate intermediate interactions that will not produce them.
summary: The paper develops a theorem to filter out Hamiltonian terms that do not affect local system dynamics. By testing this theorem on various qubit chain models, the authors demonstrate its predictive power. Crucially, they show that when the underlying commutation relations break down, 'emergent couplings' can generate entanglement between subsystems that never directly interact.
main_problem: To establish a rigorous theorem identifying Hamiltonian terms that do not affect local dynamics or observables, and to analyze when this theorem breaks down.
main_result: The study shows that while certain interactions can be ignored for local dynamics based on commutation relations, non-commuting intermediate interactions can generate entanglement between non-directly coupled subsystems via an emergent coupling mechanism.
method: The analysis uses partial tracing over environment degrees of freedom applied to the von Neumann equation, and employs the interaction picture formalism for time evolution calculations.
model_or_system: The models involve qubit chains interacting with a central local system, incorporating Ising interactions, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling, and transverse magnetic fields on environment qubits.
key_observables: Reduced density matrix ($\hat{ho}_0(t)$), Concurrence ($C(\hat{ho}_{02})$), and the presence/absence of specific Hamiltonian terms in $\hat{ho}_0(t)$.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths (e.g., $G_{12}$ vs $G_{01}$) and external field strengths ($\omega_1$).
main_assumptions: The theorem relies on specific commutation relations $[\hat{H}, \hat{H}_{E2}] = 0$; the entanglement analysis assumes initial unbiased probability amplitudes.
figures_summary: Figure 4 analysis shows that concurrence generation is maximized when the transverse field strength ($\omega_1$) is comparable to the coupling strengths, and vanishes if interactions are too weak or non-commuting terms are absent.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces a theorem for identifying irrelevant Hamiltonian terms. It then applies this theorem to simple qubit chain models (Ising/DM) where it holds true. Finally, it examines a third system where the commutation relation fails, demonstrating emergent coupling and calculating entanglement using Concurrence.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful theoretical tools for simplifying complex open quantum systems by identifying irrelevant couplings, while simultaneously revealing how non-trivial dynamics (like entanglement) can arise from seemingly 'irrelevant' or non-commuting interactions.
